story: Cyberattacks on Ukraine and Russia emergency alert apps after ceasefire ends
narration: Russia's Emergencies Ministry has reported a massive cyberattack on its mobile app, which is used to alert the population about drone attacks and other dangers. story: South Korea announces record 2027 budget with major investments in AI and semiconductors
narration: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has announced the country's largest ever budget, with total spending for 2027 set to rise by 12.8% to 820.9 trillion won, equivalent to around $610 billion. A significant portion of this budget, 21.3 trillion won, will be allocated to semiconductors, physical AI, and AI data centres, nearly doubling the investment from 2026. Additionally, 4.7 trillion won will be dedicated to developing a sovereign AI model, which President Lee described as aiming for the world's highest performance. In his annual budget address to parliament, Lee emphasised the commitment to invest boldly in artificial intelligence and future growth sectors. The overall investment in AI and semiconductors is expected to total nearly $16 billion, reflecting the administration's focus on advancing technology and innovation as key drivers of economic growth.

story: Binance resumes withdrawals after $6.3 billion hack, sees $3.64 billion net outflows
narration: Binance has reported net outflows of $3.64 billion after reopening withdrawals on Sunday, following a $6.3 billion hack. Between 6 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. UTC on November 1, the exchange processed $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits. These net outflows represent 2.1% of Binance's total assets, which stood at $171 billion as of October 28. Binance resumed withdrawals in phases starting at 6 a.m. UTC, with all 15 networks and assets included in the initial phase restored by 12:36 p.m. The FBI has attributed the hack to North Korean hackers, naming the operation TraderTraitor. Binance has stated it will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds and has covered around 95% of the affected amount, ensuring users will not bear the losses.

story: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion in Mexico City
narration: Kimi Antonelli has become Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old, securing the title with four races remaining after finishing third for Mercedes at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Antonelli is the first Italian to win the championship since 1953. The race, held at the high-altitude Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, was won by Max Verstappen, marking his second victory of the season. Antonelli finished behind Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, extending his overall lead to an unassailable 119 points. The previous record for youngest champion was held by Germany's Sebastian Vettel, who won his first title with Red Bull at 23 years and 134 days old in 2010.

story: US midterm elections: Trump rallies final push amid tight races and Democratic divisions
narration: US President Donald Trump concluded his campaign efforts in Iowa and Kansas with rallies in Salina and Dubuque on Sunday. Since early October, he has held over two dozen rallies across 19 states. With more than 54 million votes already cast, Tuesday's midterm elections are widely seen as a referendum on Trump's second term. At his rallies, Trump used Islamophobic language, referring to Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed as a "jihadist" and joking that metal detectors would be needed in the Senate if El-Sayed were elected. Trump also campaigned in Florida over the weekend. Meanwhile, Haley Stevens, a Democratic congresswoman who lost the Senate primary to El-Sayed, has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers. Polls indicate Democrats are likely to regain the House and have a chance to win the Senate majority.

story: UK households face mortgage payment rises as Bank of England expected to raise rates
narration: More than 2.3 million UK households are expected to face a sharp rise in mortgage payments as fixed-rate deals end in 2027, according to data from UK Finance. Thousands of borrowers will come off fixed contracts in the final months of this year, with 700,000 forecast to switch to new rates between July and December. The Bank of England's monetary policy committee is widely expected to raise the base rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 November, potentially the first of four quarter-point increases over the next year. Mortgage approvals fell to a near three-year low in September, reflecting the impact of rising borrowing costs. Meanwhile, the Office for Budget Responsibility has warned that household disposable incomes will fall by 0.6% next year, and Ofgem forecasts an energy price cap rise of over £400 in January.

story: France student protests continue with calls for new blockades amid school reopening
narration: Student and high school organizations plan to continue the movement started six weeks ago with new blockades as classes resume on November 2. The Union Syndicale Lycéenne (USL) and the Union Étudiante have called for blockades on Tuesday and Thursday following Saturday's demonstrations. Unef called on Saturday for universities to organize on Monday, November 2, and declared Tuesday, November 3, a 'black day' for universities with blockades across the country. Police will reinforce forces starting Monday to secure schools after violence during previous mobilizations. The government announced concessions including the progressive replacement of Parcoursup by 2028, cancellation of planned job cuts in education, creation of 500 additional posts, capping class sizes at 28 students in second grade, and 15,000 additional places in higher education. The inter-union grouping including USL, Unef, Fage, and Union Étudiante demands a 10 billion euro investment in education and higher education and the repeal of Parcoursup. Emmanuel Macron's entourage stated on Sunday that 'the time for a return to class has come' while acknowledging that such movements never end absolutely clearly.

story: UN report warns global warming nearing critical 1.5°C threshold with irreversible ice melt
narration: The planet is nearing the critical 1.5°C warming threshold, according to a recent UN report. The report warns that ice melt will have large-scale and often irreversible impacts. story: Largest pediatric early warning system launched in NHS A&Es across England
narration: The world’s largest early warning system for detecting when sick children are deteriorating is being introduced in A&E departments across England. The national paediatric early warning system, known as Pews, uses a scoring system based on vital signs to assess if a child requires urgent attention. This winter marks the first time Pews is being used in A&E, making it the largest standardised scoring system globally. More than six million children attend A&E annually in England. Pews measures vital signs like blood pressure, heart rate, breathing, oxygen levels, and consciousness, with age-appropriate charts designed for rapid decision-making. Over 90 hospitals already use Pews for inpatients, showing consistently lower cardiac arrest rates.

story: India's opposition leader Rahul Gandhi vows to increase pressure on Modi government
narration: Rahul Gandhi led a rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar. He stated that Kumar's resignation would be the first step to getting the country on the right track. story: Germany investigates after needles found in Halloween candy
narration: Needles or other sharp metal objects have been found in sweets collected by children while trick-or-treating for Halloween in Germany. Incidents were reported across several regions, including Thuringia, Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Lower Saxony, and Rhineland-Palatinate. In Nuremberg, a child bit down on a needle hidden in a piece of chocolate but was unharmed. In Baden-Württemberg, needles were concealed inside sweets, making them invisible from the outside. Police have launched investigations into attempted aggravated assault in multiple cases, but no suspects have yet been identified in connection with the needle-in-candy incidents.

story: Russia's new giant radar in Kaliningrad raises NATO alarm over military standoff
narration: Russia is nearing completion of a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad capable of monitoring much of Europe. The radar system would reportedly allow Russia to intercept satellite communications and detect aircraft movements and ballistic missiles. The radar's goal is observation of long-distance targets and early warning capabilities, though operational capability is not yet confirmed. Kaliningrad is being developed into a hub for advanced military sensors and electronic warfare systems. Russia has alerted NATO it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if the Western alliance attempted to blockade Kaliningrad. Kaliningrad is approximately 200 kilometers from west to east and 100 kilometers from north to south and reportedly can deploy up to 100 nuclear warheads.
